manual.text:
## Specific task description

Task instruction: Pick up the blue pen on the box and insert it into the pen holder on the right.

Task description: The target is the blue pen lying on the white box surface at the left. Insert it into the white pen holder beside the transparent sign on the right.

Success criteria: The blue pen has passed through the right-side pen holder opening and remains inserted. Merely hovering above the opening or resting across the rim does not count as completion.

## Execution tips

- Grip a straight section of the pen shaft that fits the pads, avoiding the clip, tip, and joints. Leave enough length on the end intended for insertion to reduce the chance of the gripper hitting the holder opening.
- The box surface limits downward gripper access. Open slightly wider than the pen shaft and use different views to confirm the fingers straddle it before closing, avoiding pressing or rolling it or closing empty against the box.
- When adjusting the pen orientation, turn it slightly where it is clear of the box and has room around it. Watch the sweep of both ends to avoid the transparent sign and nearby objects.
- Insert into free space inside the holder, aiming the pen's lower end within the opening and leaving gripper clearance from the sign and holder wall. If the tip touches the rim, lift slightly and adjust rather than pressing down.
- Before releasing, confirm the pen has entered the holder and is supported, avoiding a slip if it is still resting across the rim.

narration: I will use the piper-control skill to start only this physical-robot episode with your parameters, operate from the returned manual and live observations, and call finish_episode upon completion or inability to continue.

I have read the manual and confirmed that only the right arm is available. I am adjusting the gripper angle above the box; I will use smaller steps while approaching the blue pen and confirm it is held securely after grasping.
A pose adjustment reached a recoverable controller joint limit, and the arm stopped stably. I adjusted the approach path using the returned actual pose and will continue within this episode.
The gripper is turning to close across the pen shaft. The blue pen remains on the box surface. Next I will fine-tune the position based on the wrist camera and descend in small steps to grasp it.

The straight shaft of the blue pen is aligned between the fingers, and the final small descent is underway. Reducing the tilt resolved the controller limit; next I will lift gently to check the grasp, then turn toward the pen holder.
A light lift did not show the blue pen leaving the box, so I cannot confirm it is grasped. I reopened the gripper and am continuing small corrections to the grasp height.

The wrist camera still shows the pen in the gripper gap, but the previous closure amount suggests the grasp is too high. I am keeping the pen in place while gradually lowering and correcting the angle of both fingers.

The measured opening after this closure is about 11 mm. During a gentle lift, the pen maintained its relative position to the gripper, indicating a grasp. I will continue raising slowly to confirm, then adjust pen orientation where there is clearance.
The blue pen is off the box and hangs below the gripper. I am lifting it to a safe height above the holder, then will align with the front opening while avoiding the clear sign and existing pens.

The blue pen slipped during lateral transport and landed on the box edge; the task is unfinished. It remains visible and reachable in the live image. Within this episode, I will regrasp a thicker, straight section of its barrel and recheck stability.

The blue handle has been realigned, with the grasp point farther from the tapered pen tip than last time. I will approach in steps under 1 cm, then make small vertical and lateral movements after grasping to check it.

After regrasping, the measured opening is steady at about 15 mm, and the pen stayed between the fingers while lifting. Next I will raise it and gradually turn its longer end downward, then move it to the pen holder.
The pen remains stable at the current grasp point. Reorientation hit a joint limit again, so I continued using a reachable pose. It is still above the box and has not yet entered the pen holder area.

I have moved above and to the left of the pen holder, and the blue pen remains securely grasped. I am turning the pen more upright, then will use smaller lateral and lowering steps and release only after confirming its tip enters the front opening.

The pen tip is near the left side of the holder opening, and the gripper is still closed. I am adjusting the vertical angle so the tip enters the center of the opening while leaving room for the tip and gripper to avoid the sign.

The pen tip is near the holder opening, but the side view cannot confirm whether it has passed the front edge. I will lift slightly and adjust inward toward the opening before lowering further, avoiding releasing it balanced on the rim.

After correction, the lower end of the pen is inside the holder opening, with no visible rim contact or holder movement during descent. I will lower slightly further, release, and check whether the blue pen remains inside.

After release, the blue pen fell into the pen holder on the right and remained inside. The gripper is withdrawing slightly for verification. This conclusion is based on the live view; final success still requires confirmation by the on-site operator.
